lines.en: : I’ve got good news.
: That gum you like is going to come back in style.
: The fuck is going on here?
: They call them dreams.
: They want to help you when you’re looking for something.
: Who does?
: Where are we?
: It’s getting late.
: At this rate, you’ll miss your ride.
: She’s filled with secrets.
: The kind you can’t pull from the dirt.
: I bet you want to know what happened on the beach.
: It was a special day.
: The rain just kept falling down.
: After the sun came up, you went for a swim.
: They all said the weather was perfect for that sort of thing.
: Is this...going to be on a test?
: Did you know that Halloween is coming?
: Your clothes are looking very thin.
: You should cover them with a costume.
: It’s right around the corner by now.
: It could catch you if you keep this up.
: What can?
: That extra pair of legs.
: You wouldn’t want to miss it.
: Everyone who misses it looks a lot like you.
: Now, they’re in the clouds. Where nothing can hurt them anymore.
: I’m sorry.
: I don’t understand what it is you’re trying to say...
: Am I in danger?...
: Where we’re from, the birds sing a pretty song...and there is always music in the air.
: Let’s rock!
The imp begins to scoot around the room. She does a little jig.
: She really loves this song.
: She always said it reminded her of the door to the shed.
: What kind of gum were you talking about?
: I can’t hear you. You’re going to have to speak up.
: Is there anything else you can tell me?
: There are only two things.
: Never look inside her box.
: Never put your hands in places you can’t reach.
: I really want to try that.
: But sometimes, my arms bend back.
: Psst...
: I want to ask you something.
: Will you go tell the rabbits their secrets are safe?
: The key looks a little different this time.
: And I still haven’t worn my birthday crown.
: Were there any calls?
: Why does it open the door like that?
: I’m trying to keep my shoes clean.
: We’re running low on cheese. It might become a problem.
: I wonder if that can be fixed.
: If that’s what’s recommended.
: Are you going to get that?
: I’ll go answer that.
: Hello?
: It’s the neighbor?
: He’s always loud when it rains. I wish he would go away.
: That’s no way to talk about your uncle.
: Now, that’s just rude.
This is Rabbit family. They are made of Mother, Father, and Daughter Rabbit.
It’s normal.
: Yes.
: What do you think it’s about?
: Have you heard about the beach?
: I don’t understand.
: Yes.
: I heard that it was cancelled.
: All of it?
: Yes.
: No.
: I don’t understand.
: Just forget it.
: Okay. Bye.
: Have you heard about the beach?
: No. What happened?
: They say it was an accident.
: I’ve heard that one before.
: Do you believe it?
: There’s never a good way to tell.
: Who was it on the phone?
: I can’t hear it. Will you speak up?
: Not with those lamb legs.
: I’m not laughing.
: Daughter, have you decided what you’re going to do about Halloween?
: Will it happen again?
: They say it comes once a year.
: It sounds like a lot.
: May I make a suggestion?
: What is it?
: I can’t hear you. You’re going to have to speak up.
: What was it?
: Aren’t you thinking of moving out soon?
: Maybe I will wait for Halloween.
: Who is that?
: It looks awfully familiar, don’t you think?
: It’s about the electricity.
: Now?
: Is it working again?
: I’m hearing that noise every single night. I can’t get it out of my head.
: Things like that happen in the rain, I’ve heard.
: I’m here to deliver the message.
: Oh?
: Your secrets are safe. The key looks a little different this time.
: And what about the birthday crown?
: I can’t remember.
: Hah...
I haven’t gotten any sleep in three whole weeks.
They say these things aren’t supposed to grow that quickly, but maybe this one’s different?
The mistakes I’ve made, the scars I’ve worn, the fabrics I use to stitch her favorite quilts — every sign points in the direction this new life has already headed.
But all I want now is a chance to fix my arms.
They keep bending the wrong way.
: Don’t cry. Daddy’s here.
: Are you hungry?
: Are you tired?
: I can’t help you if I don’t know what’s wrong.
Sometimes I feel like I’ve done something unforgivable.
But what I learned when I was younger is that God always forgives those who are truly willing to repent for their misdeeds.
I’ve picked far too many fruits off of far too many trees, and the toll they’ve taken on my stomach is one for the ages.
But Halloween is just around the corner. And when each and every building is full of girls in devils’ skin, it’s easier for your sins to be forgotten.
I imagine that one day, all of this will be worth it.
These three weeks without sleep — and all of the clothes that are still so very wet — all of it will be repaired.
I’ll feel fine in my own skin. And I’ll look down at results like this and smile a smile so big that the sun will come out once more.
I’m so very tired of my life alone in the dark...
Bassinets and binkies...diapers and disjointed diatribes...and I know that I’d feel better in the company of a collaborator, but those things, they just won’t fit here.
So I’ll do this on my own — grow a flower with no vase.
There is plenty of dirt to go around.
